author: More Perfect Union
description:
Since 2023, Cleveland has been home to 100 of Flock’s license plate readers.

And on June 17, the Cleveland City Council voted 3-1 against renewing the city’s contract with Flock Safety. Meaning the contract expired as of Monday, and the cameras should no longer be running.

But the cameras are still running.
title: Cleveland ended its Flock contract. The cameras are still on.

author: More Perfect Union
description:
Henrico County, Virginia has 37 data centers – and its planning on building 17 more. 

But according to 404 Media, on June 26th the county asked schools and government workers to cut back on electricity use.

The County Manager informed county employees that as of July 1st, the electricity rate paid by the county was going up by 25% – increasing costs by about $5 million. So to mitigate the increases, county employees were asked to do things like "turn off lights" and "adjust blinds."
 
This is in the midst of a historic heat wave rocking the country. Henrico County will see temperatures rise to 100 degrees, and has issued an excessive heat warning to residents.
title: County with 37 data centers asks schools to "conserve energy"

author: More Perfect Union
description:
People in Corpus Christi are being told to cut back on their water use.

At the same time, despite severe drought, corporations are guzzling more than ever.

All enabled by Governor Abbot's corporate friendly appointees that control Texas's major water governing organizations.

Producer/Host: Kamran Rosen
Editor: @niklaak
Supervising Producer: Court Fuller
title: The REAL reason this Texas city will be the first to run out of water
